ledger.claim: The driver cancelled a rider no-show before the free wait had run out. This is an on-demand trip, so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait runs from the driver's arrival at 09:47:05 and did not end until 09:52:05. The platform's own arithmetic in the trip record puts the cancellation at 09:51:25 — 260 seconds after arrival, 40 seconds short of the free wait — and its own flag 'cancelled_after_free_wait' is false. POL-NS-21 permits a no-show cancellation only AFTER the free wait, so this cancellation was premature and the fee it produced was not earned.

POL-NS-22 charges a no-show fee only 'when the driver cancels after the free wait'. That condition precedent is absent here, and the fare ledger confirms the money moved anyway: 5.00 SGD charged at 09:51:29, four seconds after a cancellation that itself preceded the end of the free wait. A fee charged without its policy condition is a fee the rider should not carry; under POL-GEN-03 the rider who filed and is entirely right on the whole contested amount is owed the whole of it — FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD.

The arrival event, and therefore the clock the free wait runs from, cannot be displaced in the driver's favour. The GPS trace is COMPLETE, 100% coverage, 22 fixes, no gap longer than 30 seconds, and its arrival check records the nearest qualifying fix 2.73 m from the pickup point with a reported accuracy of 4 m — inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and inside the 25 m accuracy filter — with 'corroborated' true and arrival stamped at 09:47:05. Even on the platform's most generous reading, its own wait timer did not start until 09:47:10, which still leaves the 09:51:25 cancellation short of a 09:52:10 expiry.

The driver's counterparty statement — 'I waited more than 5 minutes, messaged and called' — is half true and half contradicted by his own record. The messaging and the call are on the file; the waiting is not. The trip record's own timestamps put arrival-to-cancellation at 260 seconds, and the wait timer event shows the clock starting at 09:47:10 at the earliest. The waiting time is precisely what POL-NS-21 makes the condition of the fee, and the driver did not serve it.

I do not press POL-NS-23. The contact obligation is met on this record: two driver messages at 09:47:30 and 09:49:50, both read, and one in-app call at 09:50:30 ringing 22 seconds unanswered, all before the 09:51:25 cancellation — 'obligation_met' is true. But POL-NS-23 is a separate, cumulative protection. Satisfying it does not license a cancellation made before the free wait expires, and it does not convert an early cancellation into a fee-bearing no-show under POL-NS-21.

The contact that was made came too late to be a substitute for waiting. The second message, 'Pls come down, waiting', was sent at 09:49:50 and read at 09:50:17; the single call went out at 09:50:30 and was never answered. The driver then cancelled 55 seconds after the call and 68 seconds after the read receipt, with 40 seconds still on the free-wait clock he was obliged to serve under POL-NS-21. The free wait exists to give the rider exactly that last stretch; the driver cut it off.

No fact that POL-NS-21, POL-NS-22 or POL-NS-23 needs is missing, so POL-GEN-26 escalation is not engaged and this case should be ruled on the money now. Arrival, cancellation, contact and the charge each come from a COMPLETE artifact at weight 1.0 (trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare ledger). The single absence on the file is the traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-05054-01, which I identify as MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT: it carries no fact about the waiting time and neither helps nor is needed by either side. Ruling on a no-show at this value is the AI's to make under POL-NS-26, and the record is complete enough to make it.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met in both limbs, and both before the cancellation. The chat log carries two driver messages to the rider (MSG-05054-001 at 09:47:30 and MSG-05054-002 at 09:49:50, each delivered and read), and the trip record carries an in-app call placed by the driver at 09:50:30 that rang 22 s, all of it before cancelled_at 09:51:25. The category's single fee-voiding rule is therefore not engaged, and the rider has no full-refund route on the contact ground.

The driver was at the pickup, and the arrival is corroborated on POL-NS-21's arrival test: the trip record's auto-arrival is 09:47:05, the nearest GPS fix sits 2.73 m from the pickup point with a reported accuracy of 4 m (inside the 25 m accuracy filter), comfortably within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius. POL-NS-24 gives the rider nothing: its condition precedent is that the driver failed to arrive at the pickup, and this driver arrived; the clause's 'scheduled time plus 5 minutes' deadline therefore never has to be fixed, and POL-GEN-26 is not engaged on that account.

The driver waited at the kerb rather than cancelling quickly: every fix from 09:46:50 to 09:51:20 reports zero speed within a few metres of the pickup, a stationary run of seven consecutive fixes spanning the whole period from arrival to cancellation. There is also no evidence the rider ever appeared at the pickup: the trace carries no rider track at all, so the rider's assertion that they were 'already walking down' is uncorroborated by anything in the record.

The driver does not dispute the wait arithmetic: on this on-demand trip the free wait runs from arrived_at 09:47:05 and expires at 09:52:05, while the cancellation at 09:51:25 came 260 s after arrival, 40 s short, and the record's own free_wait.cancelled_after_free_wait reads false. That shortfall is the rider's best point, but it does not void the fee. POL-NS-21 states when the driver may cancel as a no-show; it does not itself attach a fee-voiding consequence to a cancellation in the closing seconds of the free wait, and the category attaches that consequence to one thing only — the contact failure in POL-NS-23 — which is absent here.

Where the fee stands, POL-NS-22 fixes the outcome in the driver's favour: the fare breakdown records exactly one cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD charged at 09:51:29, matching the policy fee of 5.00 SGD (fee_matches_policy true), and no refund has been issued (refund_issued_sgd 0.0), so the present state is the charge. The ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both carrying the 5.00 SGD the ruling moves.

Nothing in this record requires escalation under POL-GEN-26. The facts the no-show rules need — when the driver arrived, whether he messaged and called before cancelling, and what fee was charged — are all carried by COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0, and the one absent artifact, the traffic advisory, is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) with weight 0.0: it carries no fact, and no rule in this category turns on traffic. There is no open question for a human reviewer to resolve.

Neither profile carries fraud_flags, so POL-GEN-22's raised 0.95 confidence bar is not engaged, and at a contested value of 5.00 SGD — below the 10.00 SGD band — the AI ruling on this no-show is final under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: the money in dispute is the 5.00 SGD no-show cancellation fee charged to the rider at 09:51:29 on 14 Aug 2026 (EV-FARE-05054, cancellation_fee 5.00, total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). The rider filed, contesting it. I find the rider is right, and the fee is returned in full.

Why: this was an on-demand trip with no scheduled pickup time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait runs from the driver's arrival. The platform's own trip record (EV-TRIP-05054) puts arrival at 09:47:05 and the driver's cancellation at 09:51:25 — 260 seconds later — and its own free_wait flag reads cancelled_after_free_wait = false. The free wait therefore ran to 09:52:05 and the driver cancelled 40 seconds before it expired. POL-NS-22 charges the 5.00 SGD fee only 'when the driver cancels after the free wait'. That condition was not met, so the fee was not earned and the rider should not carry it. POL-GEN-03's FULL_REFUND applies: the filing rider is right on the whole contested amount, so 5.00 SGD is returned and driver_compensation_sgd is null.

What I did not accept from the driver's side: the driver argues POL-NS-21 is only a permission and that nothing but POL-NS-23 voids the fee. It is true the driver was at the pickup — the GPS trace (EV-GPS-05054) corroborates the 09:47:05 arrival, nearest qualifying fix 2.73 m away at 4 m reported accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius and 25 m filter — and it is true the POL-NS-23 contact obligation was met (two in-app messages at 09:47:30 and 09:49:50, both read, and one in-app call at 09:50:30 ringing 22 s unanswered, all before cancelled_at 09:51:25). But the charging condition in POL-NS-22 is the free wait, not arrival and not contact; contact is a separate cumulative protection, and meeting it does not license a cancellation made before the wait expires. POL-NS-24 gives the rider nothing, because the driver did arrive.

What I did not need from the rider's side: POL-GEN-26 escalation is not engaged. Arrival, cancellation, contact and the charge each come from COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0 (trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare ledger), and the only absence, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05054-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 (MISSING_ARTIFACT) and carries no fact any rule here needs.

Procedure: the value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries fraud_flags, so this ruling is final under POL-NS-26 (the 0.95 bar is not engaged). No referral fires: the charged fee matches the policy fee of 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22's amount check adds nothing; POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not apply (the driver did arrive); and the rider's no-show count does not reach POL-NS-25's threshold of 3, so no repeat no-show flag is raised.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
